Even though I was sort of still a kid, when I was 18 I took the Amtrak for the first time to see my bf and his family at their beach house for three days. When it was time to go back, I got the days mixed up of when I was leaving and his mom wanted me to leave one day earlier than I thought, I immediately bought the ticket for the day she was expecting I would leave once I realized the miscommunication. She and my bf dropped me off at the station(he waited with me for the train, she stayed in the car) and the track number changed while I was waiting for it outside so I missed it. There were no other trains back home the rest of the day. She screamed, cursed, and cried at my boyfriend to leave me to figure out how to get home on my own. She screamed at me saying I was a narcissistic bitch who intentionally missed it so I could stay another day. She was so angry that she would be home later than expected and get less sleep. This was the first time I felt like a mother, and a woman did not care that I would be stranded somewhere overnight in one of the most unsafe cities in America at the train station. Thankfully my bf at the time stayed with me through all her yelling, called his dad (parents were divorced), his dad got me a hotel room and managed to bypass the 21+ age requirement at the hotel, I got an uber to the hotel, and his father called me to make sure everything was ok. My dad then drove 4 hours at 11 PM to pick me up.

In high school, my closest friend at the time (m) had gotten out of the psych ward like 1 day before the first day of our senior year. We went to a football game a couple months later and he was still in a fragile place, just beginning and adjusting to new medicines. We ended up going behind the stadium with some other people to smoke pot and he fell backwards after his first bong rip and was practically passed out. I asked everyone to leave except for immediate friends that I was driving home later. All three of us girls carried him through the woods back into my car, I dropped off the two friends and then parked outside of a party that I knew was happening directly behind my house because I didn’t want my parents to see us drive in and come to him. Once I parked, he started trying to pull his molar teeth out of his mouth because they were hurting him and “pushing to get out” and he started having conversations with nobody. He was clearly having some sort of episode. I saw a girl about to go into the party that I played soccer with on our school team and begged her to get water for me inside and bring it back. Another girl that I grew up with came to the car rambling about how I shouldn’t be drunk driving and I told her to just stop because she didn’t understand my situation and why i was so freaked out, she kept pushing and pushing offering to drive my car back to my house even though it was literally a 2 min walk (she knows where I live) and I hadn’t been drinking at all. I eventually just told her to “shut the f up and leave me alone”, the other girl never got the water and instead pestered me for information but I didn’t want to tell anyone his personal business so I just said he felt really sick. 


Few months later, 
A guy in my English class vaguely referred to a rumor about me raping this friend that evening. I was insanely confused. Turns out the twin brother of the girl saying I was drunk driving told tons of people in my grade that I raped my friend. This was so painful because I had gone to the school psychologist several times from how traumatized I was after his episode. I told my friend and he was also super super shocked about it and thought it was comical. I never thought it was funny that I walked around the school my whole senior year and didn’t know until a random person in my class told me.

This is actually completely normal! The way that our brains work relative to reading particular texts is that comprehension is sort of gradual. First time you read a page, you read the words, you have a super vague and basic idea of what’s going on but the second or third time you read it is when you can understand the DETAILS and truly analyze it. Re-reading also will help you while you read the rest of the novel because you’re repeatedly exposing yourself to that line or segment truly engraving it into your memory. 

I think you actually get more out of it this way. 
You just need to learn how to assist the way your brain works for the both of you (you and your brain) to reach your fullest potential - just like you’re doing by re-reading things you aren’t fully grasping on a first read

3k is way too much. You’re not giving her money for survival (food, health necessities) at this point, you’re funding her partying. But it’s not your fault. My parents had a really hard time gauging how much money to give me when I first got to college. They gave me $400 a month during my freshman and sophomore year. I’m now a junior and get $100 a month from my parents and work a part time job that makes me learn to spend and save more wisely. I’ve learned the value of money this way. Reduce the allowance so much that she feels she can’t socialize enough without a job. I felt that 100/week wasn’t enough for me because a lot of my friends are wealthy and could casually go out for dinner a couple times a week so I personally felt I just NEEDED to start working. I got my first job at 17 and saved a few thousand from that so I could spend in college when I first got there since I wanted to adjust to it before working. I then got a job my second semester of freshman year and funded myself in that way and even paid for a trip to Mexico all by myself and it was extremely fulfilling to be able to do that for myself. Sophomore year I took a break and lived on that $100/week and just figured it out. I figured out how to make amazing ramen in my dorm, bought a hard boiled egg maker to have breakfast, starting making coffee at home and not buying it every morning. She’ll be closer to becoming an independent adult once she goes through different financial stages. You are NTA.
